title: Canicule : l’ASNR modifie temporairement les prescriptions applicables aux rejets thermiques de la centrale nucléaire du Bugey pour permettre d’assurer la sécurité du réseau électrique
date_evidence: Dateline on the page above the lead image: "11/07/2026"; body: "l’ASNR a adopté le 10 juillet 2026 des prescriptions modifiant temporairement les limites applicables aux rejets thermiques de la centrale nucléaire du Bugey"
key_claim: On 10 July 2026 the ASNR adopted temporary prescriptions raising the thermal-discharge limits for Bugey reactors 4 and 5 until 20 July 2026, capping upstream-to-downstream warming of the Rhône at 1°C with reinforced ecological monitoring, because RTE judged a minimum output from those reactors necessary for grid security and the energy ministry treated that as a public necessity under Article R. 593-40 II of the Environment Code; the decision was approved by the minister the same day, and a comparable situation had arisen in summer 2022.
frame_summary: The regulator presents the waiver as a bounded exception justified by grid security and acceptable on the ecological record of past heatwaves, and stresses that its use is limited to the strict minimum RTE requires.
verbatim_quote: Cependant, le gestionnaire du réseau de transport d’électricité (RTE) estime que le maintien à un niveau minimal de puissance des réacteurs 4 et 5 est nécessaire à la sécurité du réseau électrique. Sur cette base, le ministère chargé de l’énergie considère que ce maintien en fonctionnement constitue une nécessité publique.
verbatim_list: L’ASNR prescrit en particulier que l’échauffement entre l’amont et l’aval de la centrale nucléaire doit rester inférieur à 1 °C. Cette décision est applicable jusqu’au 20 juillet 2026. L’usage de ces dispositions est limité au strict nécessaire pour pouvoir respecter le niveau de puissance requis par RTE pour la sécurité du réseau électrique.
Cette décision a été homologuée par la ministre chargée de la sûreté nucléaire le 10 juillet 2026.
Une situation comparable avait été rencontrée lors de l’été 2022. L’ASN avait alors modifié temporairement les limites des rejets thermiques de plusieurs centrales nucléaires dont celle du Bugey.

Le réacteur 3 dispose d’un refroidissement en circuit dit « ouvert », engendrant un échauffement du Rhône par les rejets thermiques de l’ordre de quelques degrés, tandis que les réacteurs 4 et 5, qui sont en circuit dit « fermé » avec des tours aéroréfrigérantes, engendrent quant à eux un échauffement du Rhône de l’ordre de quelques dixièmes de degrés entre l’amont et l’aval.

publisher: ASNR (Autorité de sûreté nucléaire et de radioprotection)
title: L’ASNR fait le point sur les conséquences des canicules et sécheresses sur les centrales nucléaires (note d’information)
date_evidence: Dateline under the tags "Sûreté / Note d'information": "25/06/2026"; the page also carries an "Ajout de juillet 2026" cross-link to the Bugey decision.
key_claim: Before the summer, the ASNR set out that if EDF asked in 2026 for a temporary change to thermal-discharge limits for grid-security reasons, as in 2022, it would have to process the request in a limited time; EDF now sends the regulator every year at the start of summer its analysis of ecosystem responses in past heatwaves and its planned reinforced monitoring, so that such a request can be handled fast; in 2022 limits were adapted at Golfech, Bugey, Saint-Alban, Blayais and Tricastin; and the ASNR will issue an opinion by the end of 2026 on the consequences of climate change for operation beyond 60 years.
frame_summary: The regulator frames heatwave waivers as a foreseeable recurring event to be prepared for procedurally each summer, and folds climate change into the question of whether the fleet can run beyond 60 years.
verbatim_quote: Afin d’anticiper une telle situation, EDF transmet à l’ASNR chaque année au début de l’été son analyse de la réponse des écosystèmes observée lors des épisodes de canicule passés et la surveillance renforcée des eaux de surface qu’elle envisage.
verbatim_list: Dans le cas où EDF serait amenée à solliciter en 2026 une modification temporaire des limites des rejets thermiques de certaines centrales nucléaires en raison d’impératifs de sécurité du réseau électrique comme en 2022, l’ASNR devra instruire cette demande dans un temps limité, en tenant compte des conditions météorologiques et hydrologiques les plus récentes.

L’ASNR a alors autorisé temporairement des adaptations des limites pour les centrales de Golfech, Bugey, Saint-Alban, Blayais et Tricastin tout en exigeant une surveillance accrue des milieux aquatiques.

Par ailleurs, l’ASNR analyse actuellement les conséquences du changement climatique sur la sûreté des centrales nucléaires et la protection de l’environnement dans le cadre de la démarche qu’elle a lancée sur les perspectives de poursuite de fonctionnement de ces installations au-delà de 60 ans. Elle rendra un avis sur le sujet d’ici la fin de l’année 2026.

title: Canicule : la sécurité d’approvisionnement en électricité n’appelle aucune vigilance particulière
date_evidence: Dateline under the headline: "22/06/2026"; foot of article: "Mise à jour effectuée le 25/06"
key_claim: On 22 June 2026 the French TSO said security of supply called for no particular vigilance: consumption would average 58 GW that week, below the 60 GW peak of 1 July 2025; each extra degree adds roughly 0.7 GW to 1 GW of demand, so air conditioning was adding 10 GW to 14 GW at the peaks; the system appeared well able to cope even with intense heatwave and drought episodes; and RTE's SDDR investment plan includes €24 billion by 2040 for renewal and climate adaptation of the grid against a +4°C-in-2100 trajectory.
frame_summary: The TSO argues that the heatwave is an operating condition the system is dimensioned for, not an adequacy emergency, and points to its long-term adaptation spending as the structural answer.
verbatim_quote: Le niveau de production est suffisant et le système électrique apparaît largement en mesure de faire face aux besoins d’électricité même en cas d’épisodes intenses de canicule et de sécheresse.
verbatim_list: La consommation d’électricité atteindra 58 GW en moyenne cette semaine, et restera en deçà du pic de consommation de 60 GW atteint le 1er juillet 2025.

Ainsi, l’effet de la climatisation se traduit par une augmentation de 10 à 14 GW de consommation en moyenne suivant les pointes cette semaine par rapport à une période équivalente avec des températures de saison.

Notre plan d’investissement (SDDR) intègre un volet renouvellement et adaptation du réseau électrique au changement climatique (24 milliards d’euros d’ici à 2040) pour maintenir un haut niveau de qualité de service tout en anticipant les impacts du changement climatique (+4°C en 2100).

title: Solar helps Europe’s grid withstand extreme heat
date_evidence: Dateline under the standfirst: "13 Aug 2026"; meta-article:modified_time: 2026-08-14T12:18:47+00:00
key_claim: Up to 29 GW (43%) of French nuclear capacity was unavailable on 12 July 2026, with at least 11 GW marked forced or environmental, so the heatwave may have affected up to 18% of French nuclear capacity against an estimated 15% in June 2025; record low Danube levels sharply cut output at Hungary's and Romania's only nuclear stations, which normally supply 40% and 15% of their generation; a Swiss reactor shut in June for river temperature; daily demand rose up to 28% in Italy, 23% in Hungary, 14% in France and 13% in Spain; day-ahead prices reached €313/MWh in France and €285/MWh in Italy on 24 June; and Hungary and Romania asked households and businesses to limit evening consumption.
frame_summary: Ember argues that record solar carried Europe through the heatwaves and that the exposed hours are the evenings, so the policy answer is battery storage and demand response rather than more thermal capacity.
verbatim_quote: record low Danube water levels have sharply reduced output from the countries’ only nuclear power stations, which typically provide 40% and 15% of their respective electricity generation
verbatim_list: In Hungary and Romania, record low Danube water levels have sharply reduced output from the countries’ only nuclear power stations, which typically provide 40% and 15% of their respective electricity generation.

A maximum of 29 GW (43%) of French nuclear capacity was unavailable on 12 July 2026, which is similar to the maximum of summer 2025 (30 GW), but significantly less than the summer of 2022, when nearly two-thirds of capacity was unavailable.
This means that the heatwave might have impacted up to 18% of France’s nuclear capacity, compared to an estimated 15% in the June 2025 heatwave.
A reactor in Switzerland also temporarily shut down in June because river temperatures were too high.

During heatwaves beginning in late June, daily power demand increased by as much as 28% in Italy, 23% in Hungary, 14% in France, and 13% in Spain, compared to the week preceding heatwaves (13-19 June), when temperatures were closer to seasonal averages.
For example, on 24 June, electricity market (day-ahead) prices in France and Italy reached €313/MWh and €285/MWh respectively – the highest in Italy since winter 2022/23.

Some similar measures have already been deployed in reaction to the nuclear outages in Hungary and Romania, albeit in an emergency manner, with governments asking households and businesses to limit electricity consumption, especially in the early evening.

title: Analysis: France’s nuclear reactors are running hot and still keeping the lights on (Michael Tadrous and Goran Calic, republished from The Conversation)
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-08-21T14:37:19+00:00; byline: "By Michael Tadrous and Goran Calic August 21, 2026"
key_claim: The authors of a 2026 Energy Policy study argue that the binding constraint in the heatwave was the legal discharge ceiling, not the reactors; France's heat- and drought-related curtailments stayed below 1% of annual nuclear output in every year but one (worst case about 1.3%), heat-related curtailment losses have fallen by roughly 90% since 2003, the June 2026 cuts peaked at about 4.1 GW or 7% of national demand, and EDF expects to spend around €600 million a year over the next 15 years on climate adaptation.
frame_summary: The academics argue that heat is a narrow, well-understood and diminishing operating constraint on nuclear, so the heatwave is a case for expanding firm low-carbon capacity rather than doubting it.
verbatim_quote: it’s that legal ceiling, not any technical limit of the reactor itself, that obliges EDF to reduce output
verbatim_list: During a heatwave, the rivers are already warm, so it’s that legal ceiling, not any technical limit of the reactor itself, that obliges EDF to reduce output.

we documented two decades of these cases: France’s heat- and drought-related curtailments remained below one per cent of its annual nuclear output in every year but one, with the worst case reaching about 1.3 per cent.

France’s historical record also shows meaningful adaptation: the country’s heat-related curtailment losses have fallen by roughly 90 per cent since 2003, as utilities upgraded cooling systems, refined operating practices and timed maintenance shutdowns for the hottest parts of the year.

title: When the rivers ran warm: how a heatwave thinned France’s nuclear export cushion (analysis by WSP)
key_claim: France exported every hour from 1 to 26 June 2026 (net 7.55 TWh) and nuclear availability averaged about 39 GW against roughly 36 GW in the two previous Junes, but the afternoon surplus available to neighbours fell from 11-12 GW in early June to 2.9 GW on 24 June, France became a net importer from Spain on the hottest days, and WSP concludes that for neighbouring systems the relevant planning quantity is the capacity France can deliver under thermal stress rather than its annual surplus.
frame_summary: WSP argues that the heatwave changed the shape and destination of French exports rather than their total, and that neighbours should plan on France's thermally stressed capacity rather than its annual surplus.
verbatim_quote: the relevant planning quantity is no longer France’s annual surplus but the capacity it can deliver under thermal stress
verbatim_list: For neighbouring systems that rely on French exports through summer evenings, the relevant planning quantity is no longer France’s annual surplus but the capacity it can deliver under thermal stress.
The afternoon surplus available to neighbouring markets fell from 11–12 GW in early June to 2.9 GW on 24 June, the hottest day of the month.

On a comparable basis, French net exports over 1 to 26 June were about 7.6 TWh in 2024, 6.9 TWh in 2025 and 7.55 TWh in 2026, and nuclear availability was in fact higher in 2026, averaging about 39 GW against roughly 36 GW in each of the two preceding Junes.
Spain swung furthest: France, normally a net exporter to Iberia, became a net importer from Spain on the hottest days, drawing on cheaper Spanish solar as its own margin thinned.

title: Canicule de juin : comment le nucléaire a permis à la France de traverser le pic de chaleur européen
date_evidence: Byline under the headline: "Publié le 9 juillet 2026 - Mis à jour le 15 juillet 2026"; meta-article:modified_time: 2026-07-15T13:57:31+00:00
key_claim: Reporting an Aurora Energy Research study of 7 July, the French nuclear society says about 5.5 GW of nuclear capacity was temporarily unavailable to respect river-temperature rules at Nogent, Bugey and Golfech; French peak demand reached 58 GW on 24 June; Belgium, without its two reactors under life-extension works, saw average 18h-21h prices near €370/MWh from 22 to 24 June and a 24 June evening peak above a thousand euros per megawatt-hour; and Germany's average evening prices reached €424/MWh with imports up about 30%.
frame_summary: The nuclear industry society argues that the fleet carried France through the heatwave with limited restrictions and kept it a net exporter, so the episode vindicates nuclear rather than exposing it.
verbatim_quote: En Belgique, privée de ses deux réacteurs nucléaires en travaux pour leur prolongation d’exploitation, les prix moyens entre 18 h et 21 h ont atteint près de 370 €/MWh du 22 au 24 juin.
verbatim_list: En Allemagne, malgré un recours massif aux centrales fossiles, les prix moyens ont atteint 424 €/MWh sur cette même plage horaire les importations d’électricité ont progressé d’environ 30 %.

Sur le parc nucléaire, l’impact est resté limité : environ 5,5 GW de puissance ont été temporairement indisponibles afin de respecter les contraintes réglementaires relatives à la température des cours d’eau.
La pointe de consommation a atteint 58 GW le 24 juin.
